requirements.text: The MultiMahjongServer will be designed to reside on a central computer (server) that is connected to a TCP/IP network and has a unique IP address.
The MultiMahjongServer will allow connections from MultiMahjongClients and communicate with them using IP.
The MultiMahjongServer will serve as a node for MultiMahjongClients.

When the user begins the MultiMahjongClient program, they will be able to choose to create a new multi player game, to create a new single player game, to join an existing multi player game, or to quit the program.
The MultiMahjongClient must send this game initialisation information to the MultiMahjongServer so that the MultiMahjongServer can create a new game.
The MultiMahjongClient must only allow players to make moves according to the Chinese rules of Mahjong as described in the rulebook, " How to Play Mah Jong ".
The MultiMahjongClient will inform the user whose turn it is to pick up a tile.
The MultiMahjongClient will retrieve other players' changes in the game situation from the MultiMahjongServer.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if another player is fishing.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if another player goes Mahjong.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if the hand has ended in a draw.
The game will end when all 4 rounds have been played or if the user chooses to end the game.
The CO must play moves according to the Chinese rules of Mahjong.
The CO will not have access to the data containing the faces of any tiles in the wall or any concealed tiles in any other players' hands.
The CO will have access to the number of tiles in the wall or in a player's hand.
The CO will be able to read any player's exposed or revealed hands.
The CO will be able to pick up tiles off the wall, discard tiles, reveal Kongs, and Chow/Pung/Kong/Mahjong.
The MultiMahjong system is to be written using JDK 1.2 (the Java development kit from Sun Microsystems ).
The CO must respond within 1 minute in both single and multi player modes.
The MultiMahjongServer must be able to handle requests in multi player mode of up to 10 simultaneous games (max 40 players).
The MultiMahjongClient must be able to calculate possible Chow/Pung/Kong/Mahjong moves (see Section 4.3.4 ) within 5 seconds of being informed of the last discard.
The MultiMahjongServer will have no graphical user interface and will be run using a command prompt.
The MultiMahjongClient will have a graphical user interface that the user will be able to interact with using a mouse and a keyboard.
The GUI is to be designed so that the user can perform all of the Level 1 requirements set out in Section 4 .
The GUI is to be contained within a screen resolution of 800 x 600 pixels.
All graphics will be in 16 bit colour.

There will be a Main Window that will contain the following game elements: The faces of the current user's tiles, The wall with the remaining tiles, The backs of the other player's tiles, Any revealed or exposed tiles from any player, The last discarded tile, Buttons to allow the user to pick up a tile, to discard a tile, to Chow/Pung/Kong/Mahjong and to reveal a Kong.
An administrator's manual, explaining how to install and operate the MultiMahjongServer, will be provided.
A user's manual, explaining how to install and operate the MultiMahjongClient, will be provided.
All design documentation and coding documentation will be maintained thoroughly during the project and delivered to the client.
Implement TLS/SSL for all client-server communication to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized interception or modification of game state data.
The MultiMahjongServer must validate and sanitize all incoming data from MultiMahjongClients, including player names and game commands, to prevent injection attacks.
Implement a basic authentication mechanism to ensure only authorized users can join games and prevent unauthorized access to server management functions.
Define specific recovery procedures for network timeouts, packet loss, and server-side state synchronization failures.
The system shall implement a heartbeat mechanism and define a state-recovery protocol for clients reconnecting to an active game session within 60 seconds.
The MultiMahjongServer shall maintain a round-trip time (RTT) of less than 200ms for game state updates under a load of 10 simultaneous games.
The system shall implement a periodic state-checkpointing mechanism to the server to allow for game recovery in the event of a server process crash.
The CO must calculate and execute a move within 2 seconds of the turn being assigned.
The MultiMahjongServer must support 10 simultaneous games with a maximum round-trip latency of 200ms for client-server communication under full load.
The MultiMahjongClient must calculate all valid Chow/Pung/Kong/Mahjong moves within 500ms of receiving the discard event on the minimum specified hardware (100 MHz processor).
